title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)
description: Overcome hallucinations and knowledge cutoffs by combining vector databases with grounded LLM generation pipelines.

slides.title: Grounding LLMs in Reality 🔍
slides.content:
# The Limits of Internal Model Weights

Foundation LLMs suffer from two fundamental enterprise limitations:
1. **Knowledge Cutoffs:** The model cannot answer questions about events occurring after its training date.
2. **Private Data Inaccessibility:** The model has never seen proprietary internal company PDFs, databases, or client records.

**Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG)** solves this by retrieving relevant document passages at query time and injecting them directly into the context window as authoritative reference material.

slides.title: RAG vs Model Fine-Tuning ⚖️
slides.content:
# Architectural Comparison

| Dimension | Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) | Model Fine-Tuning |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Knowledge Freshness** | Instant (updates immediately when documents are added to vector DB) | Static (requires retraining or re-running fine-tuning pipeline) |
| **Hallucination Risk** | Low (responses cite retrieved text verbatim) | Moderate to high (knowledge is encoded fuzzily into weights) |
| **Transparency & Auditability**| High (exact source passages cited with hyperlinks) | Low (opaque weights) |
| **Primary Ideal Use** | Factual enterprise Q&A, compliance, live search | Imparting tone, style, jargon, or specialized grammar |

quizData.question: What is the primary role of a vector database (such as Pinecone, Chroma, or Milvus) in a RAG pipeline?

options.text: To compile Python source code into C++ binaries
To index document chunk embeddings and retrieve the top semantically similar text passages for a user query
To replace the LLM transformer layers entirely
To backpropagate gradients into the pre-training dataset

quizData.explanation: Vector databases store dense embedding vectors for chunked documents and execute approximate nearest neighbor search to find text semantically relevant to user queries.

slides.title: AI Pro Tip: Chunking Strategies 💡
slides.content:
## Chunk Size & Overlap
In RAG pipelines, avoid chunking documents by arbitrary character counts. Use **semantic chunking** (preserving paragraphs or markdown sections) with 10-20% chunk overlap to ensure sentences aren't severed mid-thought!
